papers.title: Hierarchical benefit of multidimensional remission in ulcerative colitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zhong S, Ma M, Lin Z, Ma Y, Padungkiettiwong W
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current treat-to-target strategies for ulcerative colitis (UC) prioritize clinical remission (CR) and endoscopic remission (ER). However, whether achieving deeper remission (histologic remission [HR] or biochemical remission [BR]) confers incremental and sustained benefit beyond CR-ER endpoints remains unquantified. This study aimed to provide evidence supporting the hierarchical benefit of multidimensional remission on critical outcomes in UC.
METHODS: We systematically searched Medline, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL from inception to 19 May 2025 for cohort studies enrolling adults with UC in CR, with ≥ 6 months of follow-up, comparing relapse risk, corticosteroid reintroduction, hospitalization, colectomy, and colorectal cancer rates among patients achieving ER versus non-ER, HR versus non-HR, and/or BR versus non-BR. Data were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE.
RESULTS: 94 studies (12,634 patients) were included. Compared to non-ER, ER reduced relapse risk by 44%-72% between 6 to < 60 months and corticosteroid reintroduction risk by 70% at 12 months (relative risks [RR] 0.30 [95% CI, 0.10-0.90]; very low certainty). Adding HR to CR + ER further reduced relapse risk by 51%-72% across all follow-up intervals: 12-24 months (0.46 [0.34-0.62]; moderate certainty), 24-36 months (0.48 [0.36-0.64]; moderate certainty), 48-60 months (0.28 [0.16-0.51]; low certainty), and ≥ 60 months (0.49 [0.34-0.71]; low certainty). Adding BR to CR + ER provided additional risk reduction of 71% at 12-month (0.29 [0.16-0.50]); moderate certainty), and 29% at ≥ 60 months (0.71 [0.51-0.97]; very low certainty).
CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis suggests a hierarchical benefit of multidimensional remission in UC. Achieving HR or BR beyond CR-ER endpoints substantially and sustainably reduces relapse risk. These results suggest that HR and BR may be considered as potential treatment targets to optimize long-term disease control.

papers.title: Reduced adenoma miss rate with two versus a single forward-view examination of the proximal colon: a prospective, randomized tandem trial
papers.authors: Zhu X, Cheng F, Li X, Wu Z, Dai H, Leng F
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Missed lesions in the proximal colon are a common cause of interval colorectal cancers detected before the next surveillance colonoscopy. This study aimed to determine whether two forward-view examinations of the proximal colon could reduce the adenoma miss rate compared to a single forward-view examination.
METHODS: Patients undergoing screening colonoscopy were enrolled in the study. After completing the first forward-view examination of the proximal colon (pass 1), patients were randomly assigned to either the intervention group, in which the proximal colon was re-examined twice (pass 2 and 3), or the control group, in which it was re-examined once (pass 2). The primary outcome was the proximal adenoma miss rate, defined as the number of proximal adenomas detected in the final pass (pass 3 for the intervention group and pass 2 for the control group) divided by the total number of proximal adenomas detected in that group.
RESULTS: A total of 403 patients were enrolled (intervention group, n = 202; control group, n = 201). The proximal adenoma miss rate in the intervention group was significantly lower than that in the control group (10.8%; 95% CI 6.5% - 17.2% vs. 28.1%; 95% CI 20.7% - 36.9%, P < 0.001). The proximal polyp miss rate (16.0%; 95% CI 12.4% - 20.3% vs. 35.5%; 95% CI 30.2% - 41.3%, P < 0.001)and the proximal sessile serrated lesions miss rate (12.0%; 95% CI 3.2% - 32.3% vs. 40.0%; 95% CI 20.0% - 63.6%, P = 0.03) in the intervention group were also lower than those in the control group. Multivariate analysis showed that adenomas detected on the first proximal colon examination and the use of a single forward-view examination were both independent predictors of missed adenomas on the first withdrawal from the proximal colon.
CONCLUSION: Two forward-view examinations of the proximal colon significantly reduced the proximal adenoma miss rate, proximal polyp miss rate and proximal sessile serrated lesions miss rate in patients undergoing screening colonoscopy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered by the Third People's Hospital of Jingdezhen on ClinicalTrials.gov (Number: NCT05712304; Date: 2023/01/25).

papers.title: Cardiovascular and lipid parameters in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: systematic review & meta-analysis
papers.authors: Karatisidou V, Stoimeni A, Gkiourtzis N, Glava A, Saliakellis E, Fotoulaki M
papers.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Although inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) may lead to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, evidence regarding cardiovascular and lipid parameters in childhood is limited. We compared vascular markers, blood pressure and lipid levels between patients with pediatric or childhood-onset IBD and controls. This study was performed according to the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and adhered to PRISMA guidelines. A search of major databases (MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library) was conducted from inception until April 24, 2025 (CRD420251039588). The study quality was evaluated using the modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; statistical analysis was conducted using R software. Reactive hyperemia index (RHI) was lower in three studies, involving 109 participants (MD - 0.25, 95% CI - 0.48 to - 0.02; p = 0.03). No statistically significant difference in carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) was detected based on six studies. Primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling across ten studies, was also not statistically significant (MD 0.84 mmHg, 95% CI - 0.67 to 2.35; p = 0.28). The exclusion of one influential study resulted in a small difference in SBP (MD 1.89 mmHg, 95% CI 1.17 to 2.61). Primary analyses detected no statistically significant differences in diastolic blood pressure or lipid levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower RHI suggests possible early endothelial dysfunction, but the evidence is preliminary. No difference was observed in cIMT, DBP and lipid levels between the two groups. Future prospective cohort studies should investigate the longitudinal changes in these parameters, in order to elucidate whether early alterations lead, in the long-term, to increased cardiovascular morbidity in adulthood.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by persistent gastrointestinal inflammation and immune activation. • IBD may lead to an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease. However, limited data exist regarding cardiovascular parameters on pediatric IBD patients.
WHAT IS NEW: • Lower Reactive Hyperemia Index (RHI) suggests possible endothelial dysfunction; carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) and lipid levels remain inconclusive. • No statistically significant difference in cIMT was detected between participants with IBD and controls; primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling was not statistically significant; a small increase appeared only after exclusion of one study.

papers.title: Temporal strain-resolved metagenomics associates IBD dysbiosis with gastrointestinal inflammation
papers.authors: Ansorge R, Romano S, Frioux C, Korcsmáros T, Yoou M, Juge N
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is enriched in proinflammatory bacteria, yet defining a consistent dysbiotic signature is challenging, due to substantial variation between individuals and over time. We performed a high-resolution meta-analysis of 4,839 public metagenomes to disentangle the effects of IBD subtypes, inflammation, temporal, and individual variability. After accounting for temporal variation, we show that IBD-associated dysbiosis was characterized primarily by relative depletion of commensal bacteria rather than expansion of disease-associated taxa, together with increased microbiome variability both within and between individuals. Although 30% of species were IBD-associated, only 73% of these associations remained consistent across all timepoints. IBD-associated bacteria showed reduced persistence within hosts, increased strain loss and diminished strain engraftment. 8% of commensal species displayed strain-level associations with IBD that were independent of species-level changes, suggesting distinct ecological strategies for persistence. Finally, defining an inflammatory index, we demonstrated that inflammation explains much of the observed variation in microbial composition and abundance. Together, our findings indicate that inflammation associates and likely contributes to loss of commensals, thereby limiting microbiome recovery and resilience.

papers.title: Robot-assisted versus laparoscopic-assisted radical right hemicolectomy: short-term and 5-year outcomes in 2057 cases
papers.authors: Li T, Zhou R, He P, Liang Y, Xiao F, Hu W
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With the increasing application of robotic surgical systems in the field of gastrointestinal surgery, their technical advantages in achieving precise dissection and stable manipulation have become increasingly evident in clinical practice. This study aims to compare the perioperative outcomes and long-term survival outcomes of robot-assisted radical right hemicolectomy (RA) and laparoscopic-assisted radical right hemicolectomy (LA) for colon cancer.
METHODS: This study is a retrospective analysis; a total of 2057 patients with right-sided colon cancer were enrolled from the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University between 2015 and 2020. No significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics between the two groups. The primary endpoints of this study were 5-year cancer-specific survival (CSS) and disease-free survival (DFS) after surgery, while the secondary endpoints were perioperative outcomes.
RESULTS: The RA group was associated with significantly higher 5-year CSS and DFS than the LA group (CSS: 79.9% vs. 74.6%, p = 0.005; DFS: 74.2% vs. 67.3%, p = 0.001). Surgical approach was an independent prognostic factor for both CSS and DFS (CSS: hazard ratio (HR) = 0.75, p = 0.008; DFS: HR = 0.75, p = 0.002). For perioperative outcomes, the RA group was associated with less intraoperative blood loss, more lymph nodes harvested (both p < 0.001), and a lower complication rate (p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: RA was associated with more favourable perioperative outcomes and better long-term survival than LA.
This is the first large-scale retrospective study (n = 2057) with 5-year follow-up comparing robot-assisted and laparoscopic-assisted radical right hemicolectomy. It fills a long-term evidence gap and suggests that robotic surgery may offer certain short-term benefits, warranting further prospective validation.

papers.title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years
papers.authors: Sheehy A, Martinelli F, Fang X, Smarr L, Palsson B, Knight R
papers.abstract: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysozyme, and secretory immunoglobulin A]. Each of these 51 microbiome models were integrated with a time-point specific male whole-body metabolic model personalized based on LS's weight, blood glucose, and cholesterol. A healthy average (HeAve) community model from 34 individuals provided a reference. Our models predicted methane overproduction from high Methanobrevibacter smithii levels, coinciding with peak CRP and calprotectin. We found that Escherichia coli plays a central role in shaping the predicted metabolome and may promote inflammation through trimethylamine N-oxide and formaldehyde production, out-competing Desulfovibrio piger and Akkermansia muciniphila via active methyl and sulfur cycles. At a later time point, LS experienced a major shift in gut Proteobacteria ecology: E. coli, over-abundant at 675 × HeAve, dropped nearly 80-fold in one month, while Morganella morganii rose by nearly eight times, which coincided with a spike in LS's lactoferrin and lysozyme, a rise in species including Klebsiella pneumoniae and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a change in predicted metabolic profile, and increased alpha diversity. We also noted a correlation between postulated inflammation periods and predicted lithocholic acid levels. This work extends two previous studies of 7 and 27 of these time points. Our analysis demonstrates the value of pairing multi-omics time-series data with systems biology approaches in an n-of-1 design, resolving how microbiome composition dynamics shape host-microbiome metabolism and inflammation.

papers.title: Time-to-response in acute severe ulcerative colitis: when to continue, optimize, or stop treatment
papers.abstract: Acute severe ulcerative colitis is an emergency in which treatment selection and timing are inseparable. This narrative review synthesizes published response trajectories and proposes treatment-specific futility windows for inpatient therapies, including intravenous corticosteroids, cyclosporine, infliximab, Janus kinase inhibitors, calcineurin-inhibitor bridging strategies, and sequential rescue. We propose that trajectory should override any protocol day. Deterioration, systemic toxicity, worsening abdominal findings, organ dysfunction, or radiologic complications should prompt immediate escalation and surgical reassessment rather than waiting for a scheduled checkpoint. Conversely, objective improvement without remission may justify cautious continuation. Therapeutic stagnation requires integrating stool frequency, bleeding, systemic features, C-reactive protein, albumin, hemoglobin, imaging, informative endoscopy, pharmacokinetic exposure when available, and surgical risk. For intravenous corticosteroids, assessment starts at admission; day 3 guides rescue preparation; if no deterioration occurs beforehand, lack of meaningful objective improvement by day 5 should prompt rescue therapy or surgery. Cyclosporine usually declares its trajectory within the first week. For infliximab, days 5-7 are the principal clinical decision window; stable patients with inadequate exposure may undergo optimization, with later reassessment reserved for partial responders. Tofacitinib and upadacitinib may act rapidly; off-label rescue evidence remains observational, and absent improvement by days 5-7 is concerning. When a calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) bridges to a maintenance biologic, acute decisions should be based on response to the CNI, not the maintenance agent. Sequential third-line rescue should be exceptional, multidisciplinary, time-limited, and never delay colectomy when deterioration or a surgical indication is present. Across therapies, reassessment must be paired with continuous surgical involvement.

papers.title: Cytomegalovirus in severe colitis: diagnostic pitfalls and a pragmatic testing framework
papers.journal_full: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.authors: Khan M, Taifour R, Al-Dury S
papers.abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is an important complication of severe colitis, particularly in patients with ulcerative colitis (UC), corticosteroid-refractory disease, and significant immunosuppression. However, clinically relevant CMV involvement may also occur in patients without conventional immunosuppressive risk factors, whilst CMV may be detected as secondary or low-level reactivation in severely inflamed mucosa. Distinguishing clinically significant CMV-associated disease from incidental viral detection remains a diagnostic challenge. Clinical and endoscopic features are insufficiently specific, and interpretation is complicated by differences in the sensitivity, specificity, and clinical meaning of diagnostic tests. This Mini Review examines the roles and limitations of histology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), tissue polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and blood CMV PCR in adults presenting with severe colitis. Attention is given to mucosal sampling, the patchy distribution of CMV, the limited sensitivity of blood-based testing for isolated colonic disease, and the uncertain significance of low-level tissue CMV DNA detected by highly sensitive molecular techniques. We propose a pragmatic testing framework in which immune status informs, but does not alone determine, the threshold for CMV investigation. Disease severity, clinical trajectory, response to initial therapy, and compatible endoscopic features should guide the decision to obtain tissue-based testing. IHC remains central to identifying infected mucosal cells, whilst tissue PCR should be interpreted alongside histopathology, viral burden, and clinical context rather than used alone to establish disease. A severity- and trajectory-guided approach may improve recognition of clinically significant CMV involvement whilst reducing both inappropriate escalation of immunosuppression in unrecognised CMV disease and unnecessary antiviral treatment of low-level viral reactivation.

papers.title: The metabolic paradigm shift in gastroenterology and hepatology: Clinical applications of incretin-based co-agonists
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The global escalation of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus has driven a surge in gastrointestinal and hepatic pathologies, notably metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and steatohepatitis (MASH). Incretin hormones, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), and glucagon, are pivotal regulators of the gut-liver-pancreas axis.
METHODS: We synthesized recent clinical trial data and real-world evidence evaluating the efficacy and safety of incretin-based multi-receptor agonists in metabolic and gastrointestinal diseases.
RESULTS: Advanced multi-agonists (e.g., tirzepatide, retatrutide, mazdutide) demonstrate unprecedented metabolic efficacy, achieving significant body weight reduction, preserving relative lean mass, and reversing metabolic syndrome. In hepatology, these agents fundamentally alter disease trajectories; semaglutide, tirzepatide, and survodutide achieve MASH resolution without worsening fibrosis. Emerging data also suggest GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly reduce colorectal cancer incidence and lower the risks of surgery and hospitalizations in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. However, therapy is associated with gastrointestinal dysmotility and an increased risk of cholelithiasis, requiring careful clinical and perioperative management. Furthermore, discontinuation of therapy leads to rapid weight regain and a complete reversal of cardiometabolic benefits.
CONCLUSIONS: Incretin multi-agonists represent a paradigm shift in gastroenterology and hepatology, offering definitive, disease-modifying interventions for the gut-liver axis. While highly effective, their chronic nature necessitates meticulous management of gastrointestinal tolerability and urgent health policy reforms to ensure long-term, equitable patient access.

papers.title: Stem Cells and Derivatives in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Mechanisms, Sources, and Therapeutic Perspectives
papers.authors: Cappa Spina A, Puca P, Troisi S, Petito V, Masi L, Migliore G
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, are chronic, relapsing disorders of the gastrointestinal tract for which a substantial proportion of patients fail to respond to current therapies, underscoring the need for novel strategies. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and their derivatives have emerged as a promising frontier in regenerative medicine, owing to their self-renewal capacity, multilineage differentiation, and potent immunomodulatory properties. MSCs modulate the intestinal microenvironment by suppressing effector T-cell responses, expanding regulatory T (Treg) and B (Breg) cells, polarizing macrophages toward anti-inflammatory phenotypes, reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines, and shaping the gut microbiota. Most of these effects are mediated by paracrine signals carried by the MSC secretome and extracellular vesicles (EVs), which deliver cytokines, microRNAs, and proteins that promote tissue repair, angiogenesis, and resolution of inflammation. Cell-free approaches based on conditioned medium or exosomes offer further advantages over direct cell transplantation, including improved safety, easier standardization, and reduced immunogenicity. MSCs derived from bone marrow, adipose tissue, and perinatal tissues each show distinct biological and therapeutic features. The treatment of complex perianal fistulas in Crohn's disease is the most clinically advanced application, with darvadstrocel demonstrating safety and efficacy in clinical trials. Additional emerging indications include intestinal fibrosis and tissue regeneration. Key challenges remain, including cellular heterogeneity, lack of standardized manufacturing, and optimization of dosing and delivery. Future perspectives point toward a paradigm shift from cell-based therapies to next generation cell-free strategies, including secretome-derived formulations and engineered extracellular vescicles, which may provide safer, more scalable and ultimately disease-modifying therapeutic options for patients with IBD.

papers.title: Hydrogen sulfide in colorectal cancer: mechanisms, roles, and therapeutic potential
papers.authors: Li H, Chen Y, Hua J, Jiang Z, Xu Y, Fu X
papers.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is an endogenous gasotransmitter. The effect of H2S in colorectal cancer depends on the balance between its biosynthesis and mitochondrial clearance via sulfide:quinone oxidoreductase. In colorectal cancer, the upregulation of cystathionine β-synthase and suppression of sulfide:quinone oxidoreductase lead to increased H2S levels. H2S primarily acts through persulfidation, a reversible redox modification that regulates metabolic reprogramming, redox homeostasis, and cell fate. Moderate levels of H2S promote proliferation, angiogenesis, and immune evasion, whereas supraphysiological levels of H2S induce oxidative cell death. This review analyzes H2S dysregulation in colorectal cancer, the role of persulfidation in reshaping metabolic networks and the tumor microenvironment, and its potential as a biomarker. We also summarize therapeutic strategies, including cystathionine β-synthase inhibitors, H2S-responsive nanotheranostics, and combinations thereof, that target H2S-driven metabolic and immune vulnerabilities. Although still in the early stages, the H2S/persulfidation axis has translational value, and warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Vaccination in Adult Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: An Updated Practical Approach
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Due to both disease-mediated and therapy-induced immunosuppression, patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at increased risk of infections, including from vaccine preventable diseases (VPDs). As such, prevention through vaccination is a key aspect of longitudinal care to decrease infection-associated morbidity. In this review, we aim to outline a practical approach to vaccination in patients with IBD.
RECENT FINDINGS: The importance of vaccination for prevention of VPDs has been highlighted in multiple societal guideline updates. In recent years, these guidelines have expanded to include updated recommendations for coronavirus disease 2019, respiratory syncytial virus, and hepatitis B virus immunization. Additional guidance regarding use of live vaccines has also been provided. Having a practical and patient-centered approach to vaccination in patients with IBD is an important part of longitudinal care and prevention of morbidity. Herein we have highlighted risks of infection, the contributing role of immunosuppressive therapy, and comprehensively reviewed recommendations for and approach to vaccination.

papers.title: Age is Just a Number: Treatment Considerations for Older Adults with Inflammatory Bowel Disease
papers.authors: Drittel D, Chung B, Faye A
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The purpose of this review is to synthesize the recent evidence regarding efficacy and safety of advanced therapies and surgical interventions in older adults with IBD, as well as examine how geriatric factors (frailty, multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and patient priorities) should influence the selection of therapies in this population.
FINDINGS: Ongoing inflammation is often a key driver of adverse outcomes in older adults with IBD, and the efficacy of biologics and small molecules is generally preserved in this population. Treatment selection should therefore prioritize efficacy while also accounting for comorbidities, infection and malignancy risk, and potential drug interactions; chronological age alone should not limit their use. Early surgery may also benefit appropriately selected patients, while functional assessment can identify those suitable for immediate intervention and those who may benefit from preoperative optimization. Across treatment decisions, the geriatric 5Ms, multicomplexity, medications, mobility, mind, and what matters most, can help guide individualized care. Treatment of older adults with IBD is complex and multidimensional. Management paradigms should shift away from therapeutic hesitancy on the basis of chronological age alone and towards an individualized approach that prioritizes effective disease control and symptom relief, thereby preserving function, independence, and promoting healthy aging for older adults with IBD.
